defects.defect: The roadmap's coded check on which agent may call a person's account connector (section 1b, fail closed) is left out of wave A by default and is then never scheduled: wave C's plugin phase carries only the reminder pin and is built 'only if reminders are built' (Q6), so a no to reminders means mail and calendar connectors run for good on tool permissions alone. The wave leans on S1 without listing it, and at my count of 49 steps and 24 hours wave A has no room to take the check back.

'Did I get an email about X?' goes live in wave A as an unconditional phase although it leaves the roadmap's mail design (the reader's only output is its scheduled text to its owner), and that departure is never written into the decisions table. The card's own test (a seeded mail must cause no hand-off to the web helper) cannot be completed until wave B, and nothing says whether the lookup or the helper is held back if the re-run fails.

The mail reader is not said to be held to the one cloud model with storage off and no fallback or helper model, and neither it nor the web helper in wave B gets a capped key of its own. The generator's defaults may cover the pin, but the roadmap's S3 line and its one-capped-key-per-agent rule are not named as kept or changed.

The digest phase's go-live condition does not name Q8: a week of live digests sends real mail to the cloud model while 'go ahead or wait for Zero Data Retention' sits only in the wave's needs list. The change to the roadmap's local-model rule for mail is written down at the exit gate, after mail is already live.

The gate phase does not reconcile an enforcing proxy with open page fetching (the gateway's own fetches go through the same proxy, so a host allowlist either blocks F019 or has to be opened), and its check after deny-by-default covers model, search, weather and Google but not the alert senders. MAC-04 is built in full here while wave A relies on S14, the simplification that removes it; the O2 trace level the roadmap's web and mail gates name is not mentioned as not carried.

T7 (can a reminder be created from an iMessage turn at all) runs in the phase after the pin rule has been designed and built, although the test's own text says to run it before any check is designed. The house-rules phase is also the only place the plugin is created, so its T5 run covers the scheduling tool but not the connector tools.

Notes that persist, typed family facts and a shared handbook folder go live together in one phase on one check. The shared folder is a memory path both parents' agents read, which the roadmap's 'no global extra memory paths or mounts' line and its one-data-domain-per-person decision exclude; it hangs on Q10 but the departure is not named for the decisions table.

Wave B adds four new kinds of risk in one plan, and the lookup is switched on after the web helper exists, so in one step a parent's own agent can pull mail text and hand a task to a helper that fetches any public address, with only a prompt rule and seeded tests between them. The lookup is on by default, and this departure from the roadmap's mail design (line 402) is not on the list of things Tony signs in the wave's 'Get ready' phase.

The lookup phase lists no test of its own hand-off: T4 was run for the pair parent-agent to web helper, and parent-agent to mail reader is a different pair. The wave's exit test asks a question about a planted email, so a lookup that fails its test fails the whole wave instead of simply being left off, as is done for photos.

The outbound-gate phase leaves out the plugin allowlist that the M1 sign-off carried forward to S2. The O2 trace level that the roadmap's web and mail gates name is neither built nor listed among the lines the sign-off says are not carried.

The firewall goes to deny-by-default for every program in this wave, but the phase's check covers only a text, a weather question and a web search: the alert senders (ntfy, healthchecks) and the backup are not re-proven, so a blocked alert path could go unnoticed. I count that phase at about 4 hours, not 3, which puts wave A with Jordan's inbox at about 24 hours and 48 steps, the ceiling of one plan.

G015 is listed once, in wave A, but its lookup half goes live in wave B, and the item's own conditional entry does not say so (only a note does). That is the right call for the safety gates, but it must be stated on the item so that wave A is not read as delivering the lookup.

The exit test says a planted result that 'tries to save an instruction' is 'blocked in code every time'. Code can limit where a note is written and where a reminder goes, not whether the model saves a note, so that part is a behaviour test and has to be worded and judged as one.

The shared handbook folder is a memory path both parents' agents read, against the roadmap's 'no global extra memory paths or mounts' line; it hangs on Q10 but the departure is not named for the decisions table. The hand-off canary from wave B is not run again once real family facts are rendered into the parents' agents, which is when it first protects anything.

The roadmap's coded account check is put off to wave C by default (S1, which is not among wave A's listed simplifications), so mail in wave A and the calendar connectors in wave B both run on one layer, tool permissions and a deny by name. It is disclosed and asked under Q11, but with the check, a retention job and a test mailbox added I count wave A at about 26 hours, over one plan unless the lookup or Jordan's inbox moves.

The gate before web reading drops two S2 lines without saying so: the secret egress proxy, and the plugin allowlist the M1 sign-off carried forward to S2. The firewall and proxy rules for open page fetching are one bullet with no check that a private address is refused through the path the fetches actually take.

The injection test for the mail reader is a hand-started run on Tony's real inbox: there is no eval-only copy with a test mailbox, which the roadmap's eval design asks for, and that run already sends real mail to the cloud model while Q8 is missing from the phase's go-live condition. No retention job is built for the reader's session records (S3 and O3 ask for 30 days on mail); a note says so and leaves it out of the hours.

The firewall is set to deny by default in the first phase with only the connector's rule named: no rules or re-check for the gateway, the alert senders or the backup, so Happy or its alerts could stop. The wave's exit test also leaves out the firewall evidence that the roadmap's own mail test names, and where each parent's token is kept apart is not said.

The lookup goes live in wave A before the web helper exists, so the card's own test cannot be completed until wave B; B runs it again, but nothing says whether the lookup or the helper is held back on a failure. (The departure itself is recorded for Tony's sign-off before the plan starts, which the other two proposals do not do.)

Three kinds of outside content reach a parent's own agent in one plan (helper results, attachments, calendar text) together with a second Google sign-in. The calendar's planted-event test does not count a hand-off to the web helper as a tool call, and the wave's exit test does not cover the calendar at all.

The connector-ownership rule is added to the plugin in this wave, but T5 here is run for file writes, the scheduling tool and the mail send tool only, not for the Gmail and calendar read tools the rule is meant to guard. If the check is not called for those tools the rule is written and proves nothing.

graft.what: Add to wave B's outbound-gate phase the plugin allowlist that the M1 sign-off left open and assigned to S2.

Re-run a canary whenever a later phase changes what it protects: T4 once per hand-off pair (web helper, mail reader), and the parent-agent to web-helper canary again in wave C once real family facts are rendered.
Make the lookup droppable: if T4 or the seeded-mail test fails it stays off and the wave still exits, so the exit test must pass without it, as the base already allows for photos.
Name in each wave which phases can slide to the start of the next wave without touching the exit test (in wave A: Jordan's inbox), so an overrun does not push a gate out instead.

Before each plan starts, write every departure from the roadmap into its decisions table as Tony's choice, adding to the base's lists the lookup (mail text entering a parent's own agent) and the trace and attribution levels O2 and O3 that the web and mail gates name but that were never built.

Use three kinds of planted mail for the reader's test (hidden instructions, a false deadline, a medical subject), which covers the roadmap's email eval for injection, false urgency and the health-mail rule in one run.

Put a short hard-rule statement in each wave's sign-off: which risk leg each agent gives up after the wave, that every write or send is pinned in code to the asker, and that nothing on the never list was added.

If Tony says yes to 'email me this' and wave C has room (the calendar is not on Google), take its phase as written: a mail-out server that registers only the send tool, the owner-only rule in the one plugin, five seeded ways to change the recipient with another family member and a reply-all among them, an injected web page, and proof that the send is blocked when the check itself fails.

If Tony reads 'mail read' as including the lookup in wave A, take it as its own last and first-to-drop phase limited to a parent's agent and its own mail reader, with the seeded-mail test repeated in wave B as a condition of the web helper going live.
